grammar.title: Zero and First Conditional
grammar.explanation:
The **zero conditional** talks about things that are always true. We use **if** + present simple in both parts.

The **first conditional** talks about a real possibility in the future. We use **if** + present simple, then **will** + verb.

Do not use **will** in the if part. Say **if it rains**, not if it will rain.

Use **when** when you are sure something will happen. Use **unless** to mean if not.

An average student can learn this fast. If you practise a little every day, you **will** see beautiful progress, and in approximately one month it will feel attractive and easy.
examples: *If you heat water to 100°C, it **boils**.* (zero: always true)
*If it **rains** tomorrow, we**'ll stay** at home.* (first)
*If she **gets** the job, she**'ll move** to London.* (first)
*We**'ll be** late if we **don't leave** now.* (first, if second)

practice.q: Rewrite with the zero conditional: Heat ice and it melts.
practice.a: If you heat ice, it melts.

practice.q: Rewrite with the first conditional: Train hard and Sara will win.
practice.a: If Sara trains hard, she will win.

practice.q: Rewrite with unless: If you do not hurry, you will miss the bus.
practice.a: Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.

practice.q: Rewrite with when: I am sure I will get home, and then I will call you.
practice.a: I'll call you when I get home.
